note: Written by hand before any run. 'correct' is the outcome a checker keyed on qualified identities and reading Unicode identifiers must return; 'correct_findings' are the defects it must name, as KIND@file:line. 'tool_predicted' is the exit status and problem tags predicted for tools/lean_axiom_check.py by reading its code on main. Tags: SORRY, BUILD, AXIOM, SILENT, EMPTY (the two-space-indented message prefixes the tool prints).

C0.purpose: clean: unique ASCII names, every print reported, permitted axioms only
C0.justification: declared_prints gives {foo, bar}; AXIOM_LINE matches foo with only permitted axioms; NO_AXIOM_LINE matches bar; declared - reported is empty.

C1.purpose: clean: OIBridge.A.foo and OIBridge.B.foo (one short name, two qualified identities), both reported
C1.justification: Both prints collapse to the short name foo, both reports to foo; sets equal; reported has one element.

C1n.purpose: clean: as C1, but the prints are namespace-relative (`#print axioms foo` inside namespace OIBridge.A / OIBridge.B), the form most prints on main take

C2.purpose: clean: an ASCII print and a non-ASCII print (OIBridge.R.G₀_apply), both reported with permitted axioms
C2.justification: The declared pattern [A-Za-z0-9_.']+ followed by \s*$ fails at the subscript, so the R print is not declared; AXIOM_LINE cannot span the subscript, so the R report is not parsed. Declared {foo}, reported {foo}: PASS, with the non-ASCII result seen by neither side.

N1.purpose: short-name masking: C1 with the OIBridge.B.foo report removed

mutation.line: info: OIBridge/B.lean:3:0: 'OIBridge.B.foo' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

N1.justification: Declared {foo}; the A report supplies foo; declared - reported is empty, so the missing B report is masked: predicted false PASS.

N1n.purpose: short-name masking with namespace-relative prints: C1n with the OIBridge.B.foo report removed

mutation.line: info: OIBridge/B.lean:3:0: 'OIBridge.B.foo' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

N2.purpose: non-ASCII name hides a forbidden axiom: C2 with the R report's axioms replaced by [propext, Lean.ofReduceBool]
N2.justification: The R line is not parsed (C2), so its axiom list is never inspected; the A report keeps reported non-empty: predicted false PASS.

N2e.purpose: N2 with the ASCII report also removed, so the forbidden non-ASCII report is the only report in the log

mutation.line: info: OIBridge/A.lean:3:0: 'OIBridge.A.foo' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

N2e.justification: No line parses, so reported is empty and the tool takes the EMPTY branch: a FAIL, but not on the forbidden axiom. Shows N2's false PASS needs at least one parsable report elsewhere in the log, as every real build log has.

N3.purpose: non-ASCII print with no report: C2 with the R report removed

mutation.line: info: OIBridge/R.lean:3:0: 'OIBridge.R.G₀_apply' depends on axioms: [propext, Quot.sound]

N3.justification: The R print is never declared, so its missing report cannot be SILENT: predicted false PASS.

N4.purpose: control: ASCII report with a forbidden axiom (C0 mutated)
N4.justification: AXIOM_LINE parses foo; Lean.ofReduceBool is outside PERMITTED.

N5.purpose: control: unique ASCII print with no report (C0 mutated)

mutation.line: info: OIBridge/A.lean:4:0: 'OIBridge.A.bar' does not depend on any axioms

N5.justification: Declared {foo, bar}, reported {foo}: SILENT names bar.

N6.purpose: control: non-ASCII report carrying sorryAx (C2 mutated); the sorryAx rule is a token scan independent of identifiers
N6.justification: The literal token sorryAx is found on the R line whatever its identifier; the AXIOM rule does not see it (R line unparsed).

N7.purpose: control: ASCII declaration whose report names a non-ASCII forbidden axiom (C0 mutated); localizes the character-class gap to declaration names
N7.justification: The axiom list is captured by [^\]]*, which admits any character, so OIBridge.A.ax₀ is outside PERMITTED and flagged.
